title: Brushed DC motor
subtitle: Permanent-magnet · component study
limitations: Original simplified geometry. No manufacturer dimensions, exact winding layout, electrical simulation or fabrication data. Section view is an uncapped clipping plane; motion shows only which components rotate.

sources.title: Nidec: construction of a DC motor

parts.name: Housing / magnetic yoke
parts.purpose: A stationary enclosure that also provides a return path for magnetic flux.
parts.connection: Forms the stator with the field magnets.
parts.model_note: Illustrated as an open metal sleeve so the internal layout can be explored.

parts.name: Field magnet · N
parts.purpose: Supplies one side of the stationary magnetic field.
parts.connection: Works with the opposing magnet and the current-carrying armature.
parts.model_note: Pole colours are teaching labels; real magnets are not colour-coded this way.

parts.name: Field magnet · S
parts.connection: Together the two magnets establish the field in which the armature turns.
parts.model_note: Magnet curvature and spacing are illustrative. No field strength is calculated.

parts.name: Armature core
parts.connection: The armature develops torque when current flows in its winding.
parts.model_note: Three simplified poles are shown; this is not a production lamination design.

parts.name: Armature windings
parts.purpose: Carry current through the rotating armature.
parts.connection: Connected through the commutator and brushes.
parts.model_note: Copper loops show location, not exact turns, insulation, slots or electrical connections.

parts.name: Output shaft
parts.purpose: Transfers rotation to an external load.
parts.connection: Runs through the rotor and bearing supports.
parts.model_note: No coupling, tolerances or rated load are specified.

parts.name: Segmented commutator
parts.purpose: A rotating mechanical switch made from insulated conductive segments. Brushes contact the segments as they pass.
parts.connection: Switches winding current with rotor position, keeping its timing and polarity appropriate for continued torque.
parts.model_note: Three copper segments and insulating gaps are represented. Wiring and switching timing are simplified.

parts.name: Brush · supply side
parts.purpose: A stationary sliding electrical contact against the commutator. Graphite is one common brush material.
parts.connection: Brings supply current into the rotating circuit through a contacted segment.
parts.model_note: The brush block and holder are schematic; spring pressure and contact behaviour are not simulated.

parts.name: Brush · return side
parts.purpose: The opposing sliding contact completes the electrical path through the armature circuit.
parts.connection: Maintains contact while successive commutator segments rotate past it.
parts.model_note: The supply/return labels assume one chosen polarity. Reversing the supply changes those labels.

parts.name: Front bearing
parts.purpose: Supports the rotating shaft at the output end.
parts.model_note: Balls and rings are visual teaching geometry, not a specified bearing.

parts.name: Rear bearing
parts.purpose: Supports the shaft at the commutator end.
parts.model_note: Exploded positions reveal assembly relationships; they are not a service procedure.

parts.name: Front cover
parts.purpose: Closes the output end of the housing.
parts.connection: Holds the front bearing in the illustrated assembly.
parts.model_note: Mounting hardware and fits are omitted.

parts.name: Rear cover / brush support
parts.connection: Supports the rear bearing and brush arrangement.
parts.model_note: Insulating structures and fasteners are simplified.

parts.name: Supply terminals
parts.purpose: Provide the external connection to the brush circuit.
parts.connection: The brush and commutator system switches current through the rotating winding as the rotor moves.
parts.model_note: The model does not specify a voltage, current limit or wiring procedure.
